sourceChecks.claim: Inspected Microsoft caching guidance repeated-access latency/contention conditions, local/shared copies and management costs. Reuse and source-of-truth separation match the lesson.
Inspected Microsoft cache-aside numbered application lookup, database miss fetch, fill and response steps and consistency limitation. Hit/miss paths and potentially stale hits are supported.
Inspected Microsoft structured key examples and cache-aside application code. Distinct answer inputs must distinguish cache entries; a shared private-result key would reuse the wrong result.

Inspected Microsoft cache-aside write-then-invalidate and no-consistency-guarantee passages. The lesson explicitly supplies an old in-flight read that fills after deletion; tracing those separate operations verifies stale refill and supports source validation for freshness-critical decisions.

Inspected Redis maxmemory policies including allkeys-lru, volatile-lru and noeviction, and Microsoft per-entry expiration. Capacity removal may precede TTL; neither removal itself performs a database fetch. Redis approximates LRU, consistent with the lesson saying favors.

Inspected AWS local and external caches: independent fleet copies, cold process starts, common external entry, operations and availability costs. Local loss versus unavailable shared-service scope follows from those actors.

Inspected AWS thundering-herd and request-coalescing passages, cold/unavailable-cache overload discussion and resilience guidance. Sharing an in-flight fetch reduces duplicate work; limiting admitted fallback and rejecting excess protect finite source capacity.

Inspected Microsoft effective-caching repeated/slow/static/contended conditions and monitoring; AWS negligible-hit-rate unique-result warning. Reuse, staleness, miss cost and measured source-load/latency improvements justify conditional cache adoption.
